key_insight: Co-PiLOT combines a generative latent space with physics-informed black-box optimization to make inverse design feasible under expensive simulator evaluations and hard validity constraints.
engineering_relevance: For microstructure/texture design in magnesium alloys, this offers a practical route to search high-dimensional, non-Euclidean design spaces while enforcing decoder-based realism and simulator compatibility.
method: Train a ViT-based encoder with latent diffusion / transformer decoders to learn a compact, valid microstructure latent space.
Use a self-segmenting orientation codec to convert decoded images into crystal-plasticity solver inputs.
Run MERIDIAN, a latent optimizer with deep-kernel GP uncertainty, feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On ~80,000 EBSD-derived microstructure samples and a budget of 160 simulations, the ViT-FMDiT + MERIDIAN setup achieved the best target-driven score and reduced relative target error by 3–22% versus seven baselines.
watch_item: The approach depends on decoder fidelity and solver-consistent latent validity, so performance may degrade if the learned generative prior or feasibility model does not transfer well beyond the training distribution.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
